Cómo se lee la tabla periódica: How to read the periodic table
Los elementos están ordenados por número: Elements are ordered by atomic number Z, the number of protons. Each row is a period: all its elements have their valence electrons in the same shell. Each column is a group: its elements have the same valence-shell configuration and so are chemically similar. The lanthanides and actinides are shown in two separate rows so the table is not too wide.
<b>Radio atómico</b>: aumenta al bajar e: Atomic radius: increases going down a group, because shells are added, and decreases to the right across a period, because the effective nuclear charge grows.
<b>Energía de ionización</b>: la energía: Ionization energy: the energy needed to remove the outermost electron. It follows the opposite trend to the radius: it grows going up and to the right, with the maximum at the noble gases.
<b>Electronegatividad</b>: la tendencia: Electronegativity: the tendency to attract the electrons of a bond. It grows going up and to the right; fluorine is the most electronegative (3.98 on the Pauling scale).
<b>Afinidad electrónica</b>: la energía: Electron affinity: the energy released when an electron is gained. It is large for the halogens (chlorine, 349 kJ/mol, more than fluorine), while noble gases and alkaline earth metals do not form stable anions.
<b>Carácter metálico</b>: crece hacia ab: Metallic character: grows going down and to the left. The metalloids form the border between metals and nonmetals.
Durante años se discutió si debajo del i: For years there was debate about whether lanthanum and actinium or lutetium and lawrencium go below yttrium. IUPAC recommends (2021 report) Sc, Y, Lu and Lr in group 3, with La–Yb and Ac–No in the f block, which then has 14 columns. Here the 15 lanthanides and 15 actinides are drawn in their separate rows, as in many textbooks; the card for La, Ac, Lu and Lr notes this.
La ficha muestra la configuración del es: The card shows the ground-state configuration according to Madelung's rule (filling order by n + l), with the well-known exceptions such as chromium ([Ar] 3d⁵ 4s¹) or copper ([Ar] 3d¹⁰ 4s¹), and the distribution of electrons by shell.
Masas atómicas: valores abreviados de la: Atomic masses: abridged IUPAC values; in square brackets, the mass number of the most stable isotope. Radii: calculated by Clementi and Raimondi (1967). The heaviest elements have no measured properties.

Aquí el lantano va en el bloque f, con l: Here lanthanum goes in the f block, with the lanthanides. According to the IUPAC recommendation group 3 is Sc, Y, Lu, Lr; many textbooks put La and Ac there instead. Its configuration, [Xe] 5d¹ 6s², has no 4f electrons.
Aquí el actinio va en el bloque f, con l: Here actinium goes in the f block, with the actinides. According to the IUPAC recommendation group 3 is Sc, Y, Lu, Lr; many textbooks put La and Ac there instead.
El lutecio cierra los lantánidos con la: Lutetium closes the lanthanides with the 4f subshell full ([Xe] 4f¹⁴ 5d¹ 6s²). That is why IUPAC puts it in group 3, below yttrium; many textbooks put lanthanum there.
El laurencio cierra los actínidos. Como: Lawrencium closes the actinides. Like lutetium, IUPAC puts it in group 3; many textbooks put actinium there.
